story_review.one_viewing_summary: The intended chain, reconstructed from the executable code: A generic drone's station opens on a caliche Permian pad and the drone lifts and flies out over the equipment while a Texas card pins the Permian and Austin. The companies' blue 'Anomaly' flag rises on a pump-pressure reading, tagged 'The companies say'. Under an 'Illustration of EPA's method' chip, an approval letter lands on an inspector's desk and takes its September 30th, 2025 date and Approved marks while she watches. On her wall monitor the drone flies its plan to a valve ring and an illustrative infrared view opens. At the review screen she traces the shimmer with her stylus, presses a green confirmation and flicks a follow-up tag to the valve. In her document holder the protocol title highlights AI once. A separate, disclosed program, with no inspector present, is delayed to January 22nd, 2027 and proposed for rescission on October 7th. Back in her room she re-presses her green mark beside an empty AI box as the station closes outside her window.
story_review.opening_to_ending: It opens on the machine and the companies' claim with no person, then hands every step of the approved method to one visible person, and ends with that person's confirmation beside an empty AI box. The question 'who decides' is answered by a performed human action, and the example boundaries (pilot, approved method, separate program) are disclosed on screen and not crossed by the person.
story_review.weakest_transition: s2 to s3 (11.44 s). This is the switch from the pilot claim to EPA's method. It is honest and disclosed, but it changes setting from the screen-only pilot world to the inspector's room at the same cut, so the viewer must absorb both a new source example and a new place at once. Check at phone scope that the chip and the letter arrival read together.
